mainTopic: Blemished קדשים: blemish before or after הקדש, and the גמרא's inferences about unredeemed animals and their offspring
overview: This משנה compares two kinds of blemished קדשים. If the animal had a permanent blemish (מום קבוע) before it was consecrated, only its value is holy (קדושת דמים). Once redeemed, it becomes fully חולין: it is subject to בכורה and מתנות, may be shorn and worked, and has no כרת for slaughtering outside, no תמורה, and no burial requirement. בכור and מעשר are the exceptions. If the הקדש came first, or there was only a temporary blemish at the time of הקדש, the body itself is holy (קדושת הגוף), and the opposite, stricter rules apply even after redemption. The גמרא then reads the first case closely. Before redemption, the animal is exempt from בכורה and מתנות, and it may not be shorn or worked. A suggested proof from this for רבי אליעזר about קדשי בדק הבית is rejected: the ban may be only a rabbinic גזירה for altar animals, which people could confuse with קדושת הגוף. Finally, the גמרא explains that the permitted offspring are ones conceived before redemption and born after it. Offspring born before redemption are forbidden.

steps.title: Blemish before consecration: once redeemed, the animal is fully ordinary
steps.stepSummary: If a permanent blemish came before the הקדש and the animal was redeemed, it is treated like a regular animal. It is subject to בכורה and מתנות, may be shorn and worked, and its offspring and milk are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Take any sacrificial animal that had a permanent blemish before it was consecrated. Once it was redeemed, it is obligated in בכורה and in the priestly gifts. It goes out to ordinary status so it can be shorn and used for work. Its offspring and milk are permitted after its redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the first case: an animal that was already permanently blemished when it was consecrated. It then lists how completely ordinary that animal becomes once it is redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A permanently blemished animal can never go on the מזבח. So consecrating it only makes its money value holy, not its body. Once redeemed, nothing holy is left, and every 'ordinary animal' rule applies to it: בכורה for its future firstborn, the כהן's gifts when slaughtered, shearing, work, offspring and milk.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the text being studied)
A permanent blemish that disqualifies an animal from the מזבח forever
Consecration; making something holy for the בית המקדש
They were redeemed (their holiness was transferred onto money)
The priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal: the foreleg, jaw and maw (זרוע, לחיים, קיבה)
To be shorn and to be worked; normally forbidden with holy animals

steps.confusionAlert: 'חייבין בבכורה' does not mean the animal itself becomes a בכור. It means this animal now counts as ordinary, so its own firstborn offspring will have בכור status.
steps.whyThisMatters: Everything in this משנה depends on one question: was the animal's body ever holy? When the blemish came first, the body was never holy, and that is why all the lenient results follow.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
All sacrificial animals
in which a permanent blemish preceded their consecration
phrases.notes: Only their value is holy (קדושת דמים)

phrases.english: and they were redeemed, are obligated in the firstborn and in the priestly gifts,
phrases.notes: Their offspring can be a בכור, and the כהן receives the gifts when they are slaughtered

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁקָּדַם מוּם קָבוּעַ לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A redeemed animal that was blemished before its הקדש becomes fully חולין. It is subject to בכורה and מתנות, may be shorn and worked, and its offspring and milk are permitted.

steps.title: More leniencies for the first group, except בכור and מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The same first group carries no כרת for slaughtering outside the עזרה, does not create תמורה, and may be redeemed even after death. בכור and מעשר are the exceptions.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who slaughters them outside the Temple is exempt. They do not make a substitute animal holy. If they died, they may be redeemed. This excludes the בכור and the מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the list of leniencies for the first group (blemish before הקדש). It then carves out two exceptions, בכור and מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these rules applies only to an animal whose body is holy, so none of them applies here. There is no כרת for שחוטי חוץ. There is no תמורה. A dead animal can be redeemed and given to the dogs instead of being buried. בכור and מעשר are different: their holiness comes by itself, through birth or counting, so even a blemished one has holiness of the body.

keyTerms.meaning: One who slaughters them outside the עזרה (שחוטי חוץ); normally punishable by כרת
A substitute animal. Normally, swapping a holy animal makes the new one holy too
They may be redeemed (even after death, so no burial is needed)
A firstborn male animal, holy from birth
Animal tithe; every tenth animal is holy

steps.confusionAlert: 'חוץ מן הבכור ומן המעשר' does not mean those two are lenient. It means they do NOT belong to this lenient group, because they have built-in holiness even when blemished.

phrases.english: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt,
and they do not render a substitute consecrated,
and if they died, they may be redeemed,
phrases.notes: They are not buried; they can be redeemed and fed to dogs

phrases.english: except for the firstborn and the tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of leniencies for the same first case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals blemished before their הקדש carry no שחוטי חוץ liability, create no תמורה, and may be redeemed after death. בכור and מעשר are excluded from this group.

steps.title: Consecration before the blemish: even after redemption, the animal is not fully ordinary
steps.stepSummary: Now the opposite case: the הקדש came first, or there was only a temporary blemish at the time of הקדש. Even after redemption, the animal is exempt from בכורה and מתנות and may not be shorn or worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take any animal whose consecration came before its blemish, or one that had a temporary blemish when consecrated and later developed a permanent blemish, and was then redeemed. It is exempt from בכורה and from the priestly gifts. It does not go out to ordinary status to be shorn and worked.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה switches to the second, contrasting case. It begins listing the stricter rules that apply when the body of the animal was holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A temporary blemish is treated like no blemish, since the animal could still have been fit for the מזבח. So in both cases the body itself became holy. Redemption permits eating it, but it does not erase every trace of holiness. That is why the ordinary-animal rules (בכורה, מתנות) do not apply, and shearing and work stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary blemish that can heal
Holiness of the body itself (not just of its value)
Exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Being exempt from בכורה and מתנות is not a leniency that makes the animal 'more ordinary.' It happens because the animal is still partly holy, and these obligations only apply to fully ordinary animals.

phrases.english: And all whose consecration preceded their blemish,
or a temporary blemish preceded their consecration,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְאַחַר מִכָּאן נוֹלַד לָהֶן מוּם קָבוּעַ לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן
phrases.english: and afterward a permanent blemish developed in them, after their consecration,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִפְדּוּ — פְּטוּרִין מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה וּמִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת,
phrases.english: and they were redeemed, they are exempt from the firstborn and from the gifts,
and they do not go out to non-sacred status, to be shorn and to be worked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the contrasting case, mirroring step 1 rule by rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the הקדש preceded a permanent blemish, the redeemed animal is exempt from בכורה and מתנות and may not be shorn or worked.

steps.title: More stringencies for the second group: offspring, milk, כרת, תמורה, burial
steps.stepSummary: For the second group, offspring and milk are forbidden, slaughtering outside carries כרת, they create תמורה, and if they die they must be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their offspring and milk are forbidden after their redemption. One who slaughters them outside is liable. They make a substitute animal holy. If they died, they must be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the second list. Each ruling is the exact opposite of the matching ruling in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the body was holy, the full laws of קדשים still apply. Offspring and milk carry the holiness. Slaughtering outside is real שחוטי חוץ. A swap creates תמורה. If the animal dies before redemption, it cannot be redeemed, since a dead animal cannot be 'stood and valued,' so it must be buried.

keyTerms.meaning: Their offspring and their milk
Liable (here, to כרת)
They must be buried

steps.whatToRemember: The single key question is which came first, the הקדש or the permanent מום. Blemish first: only the value is holy, and after redemption the animal is fully חולין. Holiness first, or only a temporary blemish at the time: the body is holy, and even after redemption the קדשים restrictions (shearing, work, offspring, milk, תמורה, burial) stay in place.
steps.whyThisMatters: The two lists mirror each other line by line, which makes this משנה a model of the distinction between קדושת דמים and קדושת הגוף. The גמרא will build on this.

phrases.english: and their offspring and their milk are prohibited after their redemption,
and one who slaughters them outside is liable,
and they render a substitute consecrated,
and if they died, they must be buried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second list, mirroring step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For animals consecrated before their blemish, offspring and milk are forbidden, there is liability for שחוטי חוץ, they create תמורה, and they must be buried if they die.

steps.title: Before redemption, these animals are exempt from firstborn and gifts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה's word 'redeemed' that, before redemption, the animal is exempt from בכורה and מתנות. It concludes that the תנא holds קדושת דמים removes these obligations.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The reason they are subject to the firstborn laws and the gifts is that they were redeemed. This implies that if they were not redeemed, they are exempt from the firstborn laws and from the gifts. This shows the תנא holds that sanctity of monetary value pushes an animal out of the firstborn laws and the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה carefully. Since the משנה says these obligations apply only once the animal is redeemed, it follows that before redemption they do not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These animals had a permanent blemish before they were consecrated, so they were never fit to be offerings. They only hold קדושת דמים, meaning their value belongs to הקדש. Even so, the גמרא learns that this weaker holiness is still strong enough to exempt them from בכורה and מתנות while it lasts.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason (introduces a close reading of the wording)
But this implies (the reverse case)
Holiness of monetary value only. The animal is not fit for the altar; only its worth belongs to הקדש.
Pushes away, exempts
The priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal: foreleg, cheeks, and stomach

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two groups from the משנה. This step is about the FIRST group, where the blemish came before the consecration. Even these animals are exempt while they are still unredeemed.

phrases.english: GEMARA
The reason is that they were redeemed;
but if they were not redeemed —
they are exempt from the firstborn laws and from the gifts.
He (the תנא) holds: sanctity of monetary value
pushes away (exempts) from the firstborn laws and from the gifts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the first case of the משנה (Step 1).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before redemption, an animal with only קדושת דמים is exempt from בכורה and מתנות.

steps.title: Suggested support for רבי אליעזר on shearing and working
steps.stepSummary: From the word 'redeemed,' the גמרא infers that unredeemed animals may not be shorn or worked. It suggests this supports רבי אליעזר, who forbids shearing and working קדשי בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they go out to non-sacred status...' The reason is that they were redeemed. This implies that if they were not redeemed, shearing and labor are forbidden. Does this support רבי אליעזר, who says animals consecrated for Temple upkeep are forbidden to be shorn or worked?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a second close reading: before redemption, shearing and working are forbidden. It then offers this as a proof for רבי אליעזר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal dedicated to בדק הבית also holds only value-holiness, just like these blemished animals. So if the משנה forbids shearing and working animals with קדושת דמים, the same should apply to בדק הבית animals. That is exactly what רבי אליעזר says.

keyTerms.meaning: They go out to non-sacred (ordinary) status
Shearing the wool and using the animal for work
This supports him
Items consecrated for the upkeep of the Temple building, not for the altar
The תנא who forbids shearing and working בדק הבית animals

phrases.english: (The משנה said:) 'And they go out to non-sacred status, etc.'
The reason is that they were redeemed; but if they were not redeemed —
they are forbidden in shearing and labor.
This supports רבי אליעזר,
who said: animals consecrated for Temple upkeep
are forbidden in shearing and labor?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of close reading to the next phrase of the משנה, then draws a proof from it.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's ruling that קדשי בדק הבית are forbidden in shearing and labor.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from the משנה that unredeemed animals with קדושת דמים are forbidden in shearing and labor.

steps.title: Rejection: the ban applies only to altar animals, which can be confused
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The ban on altar animals with value-holiness may be a rabbinic גזירה, because people could confuse them with animals of קדושת הגוף. בדק הבית animals carry no such risk.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: No. Only value-holiness for the altar can be confused with bodily holiness for the altar, so the Rabbis made a decree about those animals. But animals consecrated for Temple upkeep — no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof for רבי אליעזר. It gives a reason why the משנה's ban may not extend to בדק הבית animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our blemished animals were consecrated for the altar. People might mix them up with real, unblemished altar offerings, which hold קדושת הגוף and may not be shorn by Torah law. So the Rabbis forbade shearing these too. A בדק הבית animal was never connected to the altar, so there was no reason for such a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: They say (introduces an answer)
Bodily holiness: the animal itself is holy and fit to be offered
Can be confused or mixed up
The Rabbis made a protective decree

steps.whyThisMatters: This rejection suggests that the ban on shearing and working an animal blemished before its הקדש, while it is still unredeemed, may be only a rabbinic גזירה, not a Torah law. It would be a safeguard against confusing it with an altar animal that has קדושת הגוף. Since it may only be a גזירה, the משנה cannot prove רבי אליעזר's view.

phrases.english: They say: No,
it is value-holiness for the altar
that can be confused with bodily holiness for the altar,
so the Rabbis decreed about them,
but animals consecrated for Temple upkeep — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof for רבי אליעזר. The inference from the משנה about altar animals still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed all value-holiness is the same. In fact, altar value-holiness has a special risk of confusion that led to a rabbinic decree.

steps.title: Which case of offspring does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the משנה means when it permits the offspring. It rules out a calf conceived after redemption, since that case is too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Their offspring and their milk are permitted...' What is the case? If you say the animal became pregnant and gave birth after its redemption, that is obvious: the offspring is non-sacred!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact case behind the משנה's rule that the offspring are permitted. It tests the simplest possible case and rejects it as too obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the calf was conceived and born after the mother was redeemed, it never had any connection to הקדש. A משנה would not need to tell us something that plain. So the case must be something less obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: Their offspring and their milk
What is the case? What are the circumstances?
If you say (proposes a possible case)
It is obvious (why would we need to be told?)
Redemption

phrases.english: (The משנה said:) 'Their offspring and their milk are permitted, etc.'
What are the circumstances?
If you say that it became pregnant and gave birth
after their redemption —
that is obvious; they are non-sacred!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה (offspring and milk).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what exact case does the משנה permit the offspring of these redeemed animals?

steps.title: The case: conceived before redemption, born after
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה means a calf conceived before redemption and born after it. Even that calf is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where the animal became pregnant before its redemption and gave birth after its redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case of the משנה. The calf was conceived while the mother was still consecrated, but born after she was redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the new point. Even though the calf began while its mother was still הקדש, it is permitted, because it was born after the redemption. That makes the משנה's statement meaningful rather than obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: Became pregnant (was conceived)
Was born
Before their redemption

steps.whatToRemember: For the first group (blemish before הקדש): before redemption, the animal is exempt from בכורה and מתנות, and it may not be shorn or worked. The shearing and work ban may be only a rabbinic גזירה for altar animals, so it does not prove רבי אליעזר's view. After redemption, even a calf conceived before redemption and born after it is permitted.

phrases.english: Rather, where it became pregnant before their redemption,
and gave birth after their redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8 after the obvious case was ruled out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה refers to offspring conceived before redemption and born after redemption. Even these are permitted.

steps.title: Offspring born before redemption are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that a calf born before the mother was redeemed is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they were born before their redemption, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה's ruling in reverse. If offspring born after פדיון are permitted, then offspring born before פדיון must be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said that a calf conceived before redemption but born after it is permitted. The phrase הָא לִפְנֵי introduces the opposite case: a calf born while the mother was still holy and unredeemed. That calf takes on the mother's holiness, so it may not be used until it is redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But this'. It introduces an inference from the opposite case.
Before their redemption
They are forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: The birth is what counts. Born after פדיון, the calf is permitted. Born before פדיון, it is forbidden until it is redeemed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 9. Step 9 is about a calf conceived before redemption but born after it. This step is about a calf born before redemption.

phrases.english: But if they were born before their redemption
phrases.notes: An inference from the opposite of the משנה's case.

phrases.english: they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the permitted case, the גמרא now states the contrasting forbidden case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offspring born before the mother's redemption are forbidden until they are redeemed.
